en.title: 7. Participant Re-Registration & On-Site Check-In
en.excerpt: A comprehensive guide to on-site participant re-registration, QR code scanning, batch contingent check-ins, attendance audit reports, and downstream competition impact.
en.content:
1. What is On-Site Re-Registration (Check-In)?

On-Site Re-Registration (Registrasi Ulang / Check-In) is the mandatory on-venue verification process where archers confirm their physical presence at the tournament location before competition matches begin.

While online registration and payment secure an athlete's slot in the tournament roster, on-site re-registration serves critical administrative and operational purposes:

  • Physical Attendance Verification: Validating that registered athletes have arrived on site and are ready to compete.
  • Equipment Inspection (Pemeriksaan Alat): Confirming that bows, arrows, and safety gear comply with World Archery / Perpani regulations.
  • Accreditation & E-Ticket Exchange: Issuing athlete field badges, back numbers, and official tournament credentials.
  • Target Line Finalization: Enabling organizers to identify absentees (DNS - Did Not Start) before printing scoresheets or running scoring devices.

In the Archeris database, re-registration status is tracked on the tournament_participants entity via the last_reregistration_at timestamp. When this value is populated, the participant is classified as Checked-In (Sudah Registrasi Ulang); when null, they remain Pending Check-In (Belum Registrasi Ulang).

2. How Re-Registration Status Changes (Actions & Triggers)

A participant's re-registration status transitions through four primary actions across the Archeris platform:

  1. Method 1: QR Code Scanner at Venue Desk (Recommended)

    Panitia (organizer marshal) scans the athlete's digital E-Ticket QR code from their mobile screen or printed pass using the Archeris camera scanner or dedicated mobile organizer app. Endpoint: POST /tournaments/reregister.

  2. Method 2: Batch Check-in by Contingent / Club (Check-In Kolektif)

    For large contingents with 20+ archers arriving together, the tournament manager can select the club name or check multiple participants on the Participants Dashboard (/dashboard/organizer/tournaments/[id]/participants) and execute a single-click collective check-in. Endpoint: POST /tournaments/:id/checkin/batch.

  3. Method 3: Manual Toggle in Participant Detail Modal

    Organizers can open any participant profile card on the web dashboard and manually toggle the Check-In di Venue switch on or off. Setting it to off resets last_reregistration_at to null if an athlete mistakenly checked in. Endpoint: PUT /tournaments/:id/participants/:participantId.

  4. Method 4: Mobile Manual Check-In

    Field marshals using the Archeris Mobile App can tap the check-in button next to an athlete's name in the on-field participant roster. Endpoint: POST /mobile/tournaments/:id/participants/:participantId/manual-checkin.

Payment Prerequisite Gate: The system enforces that only participants with a verified payment status (paid or lunas) can be checked in. Unpaid or pending registrations cannot be marked as re-registered until payment is reconciled.

3. Scanning Athlete E-Ticket QR Codes

Every paid participant receives a unique encrypted E-Ticket containing an identity barcode and QR payload (qr_raw). When scanned by an authorized tournament organizer:

  1. The system validates that the QR code matches an authentic participant record in the tournament.
  2. The organizer's permission is authenticated (only the event organizer or system administrators can check in archers).
  3. The system automatically executes a bulk timestamp update for all individual division entries associated with that archer in the championship, so an archer competing in multiple categories (e.g., Recurve Individual and Compound Mix) is fully checked in with one scan.
  4. Instant visual feedback appears on the scanner screen displaying the athlete's verified photo, full legal name, registered club, division, and category.

4. Collective Batch Check-In & Manual Overrides

During peak morning registration hours before the official practice session, scanning individual QR codes for large school teams or provincial delegations can create queues. Archeris provides Batch Check-In (Check-In Kolektif):

  • Navigate to Dashboard Organizer > Participants.
  • Click the Check-in Kolektif button in the top action bar.
  • Select the contingent/club from the dropdown list.
  • Click Konfirmasi Check-in. The system instantly verifies all paid athletes of that club in a single atomic database transaction.

5. System Impact & Downstream Competition Rules

Re-registration is not merely an attendance counter; it directly impacts and safeguards multiple downstream tournament features:

  • Participant Deletion & Kick Protection:

    Once a participant is marked as re-registered (last_reregistration_at IS NOT NULL), the system strictly forbids organizers or admins from deleting or kicking the athlete from the tournament roster. This prevents accidental removals during active field operations.

  • Target Assignment & Scoring Lineup (DNS Prevention):

    Field managers use the check-in filter to assign physical target butt allocations (e.g., Target 12A, Target 12B). Archers who have not completed on-site re-registration by the close of inspection can be flagged as DNS (Did Not Start), preventing empty positions and phantom scoring sheets on digital scorekeeper tablets.

  • Elimination Bracket Seeding Integrity:

    If an archer qualifies during morning rounds but fails to report or re-register for the afternoon elimination stage, organizers can audit their check-in log before confirming bracket bye advancements.

  • Official Attendance & Event Certificates:

    Verified certificates of participation and official attendance attestations rely on the last_reregistration_at record to prove physical presence at the championship.

6. Attendance Analytics & Audit Logs

Organizers can monitor field attendance in real time through dedicated reporting panels:

  • Attendance Reports (/dashboard/organizer/tournaments/[id]/reports/attendance): Displays the overall check-in rate (e.g., 94% Checked-In), checked-in vs pending counts, and arrival trends by hour.
  • Recent Check-In Logs: A live chronological audit stream showing exact check-in timestamps, club names, and division breakdowns as athletes pass the inspection desk.
  • CSV Attendance Export: Download official attendance rosters containing timestamps, payment statuses, and category entries for event sponsors and governing bodies.

7. Best Practices & Troubleshooting FAQ

Q: Can an archer enter scores if they haven't re-registered?

A: While scorekeeper tablets display archers assigned to targets, official tournament rules require organizers to finalize target assignments based only on checked-in athletes. Unverified archers should not be assigned targets to avoid invalid match logs.

Q: Can an organizer undo a check-in if made by mistake?

A: Yes. In the Participant Detail view on the Organizer Dashboard, toggle the Check-In di Venue switch to "Belum Registrasi Ulang". This resets the timestamp back to null.

Q: What if an athlete's phone has no internet at the venue?

A: Archers can show a saved screenshot or printed copy of their QR code. Organizers can also search by athlete name in the participant search bar and perform a 1-click manual check-in.
